questions.subject: Civil Engineering
questions.questionMarkup:
Consider the following differential equation:

 
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
questions.questionText: Consider the following differential equation: Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.html: The degree of the equation is not defined.
options.text: The degree of the equation is not defined.

options.html: The order of the equation is 2.
options.text: The order of the equation is 2.

options.html: The order of the equation is not defined.
options.text: The order of the equation is not defined.

options.html: The degree of the equation is 2.
options.text: The degree of the equation is 2.

questions.explanationHtml:
(a, b)
The degree of the differential equation is the power of the highest order derivative whereas the order of the differential equation is the order of the highest order derivative present in the equation. Thus, given differential equation has the order 2. Since, the given differential equation cannot be written as a polynomial in all the differential coefficients, the degree of the equation is not defined.
